12.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
12.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
13.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

14.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
14.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
14.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

15.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
15.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

16.meaning: The diversion / the idle amusement — the specific distraction or entertainment previously referred to; worldly diversion that competes with spiritual attention.
16.grammar: A definite masculine noun in the genitive case, marked by the final -i. The genitive indicates the word follows a preposition or is the second part of a possessive chain (iḍāfa), linking it to a governing noun or preposition that precedes it.
16.root: ل-ه-و (l-h-w) — to be diverted, to play idly, to distract

17.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
17.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

18.meaning: The transaction / the trade — buying and selling, commercial dealing; specifically the business activity that can compete with one's attention during the call to worship.
18.grammar: A definite feminine noun on the fiʿāla pattern (فِعَالَة), in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive indicates the word is governed by a preposition or is the second element of a possessive construction. The lam of the article assimilates to the solar tāʾ.
18.root: ت-ج-ر (t-j-r) — to trade, engage in commerce

19.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
19.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
19.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

20.meaning: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
20.grammar: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
20.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

21.meaning: The providers / the bestowers of sustenance — those who supply and sustain; when applied to Allah, it is one of His attributes: the One who gives provision to all creation without limit or equal.

parts.en: the providers / those who give sustenance (active participle, masculine plural, genitive/accusative)

21.grammar: A definite active participle (ism fāʿil) of Form I, masculine sound plural, in the genitive or accusative case. The sound masculine plural in non-nominative (genitive/accusative) takes the single, unanalysable -īna ending. It functions as a superlative-like title in a comparative phrase ('the best of providers') — the definite plural participle naming the supreme category.
21.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, to give sustenance and livelihood
